newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh and India have agreed to further strengthen ties and forge greater understanding on crucially important issues like ending cross-border insurgtency.

Visiting Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said in an interview with Bangladesh Television last night that more than 95 percent of the Indian people have welcomed the Ganges water sharing treaty with Bangladesh.

Bangladesh can initiate further talks with Myanmar to crystalise the intention of the latter to open a new direct international route between Dhaka and Yangoon, said Dr. Rahmatullah, ESCAP Director for transport, communication and tourism.
Secretary-General of main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, has said the government is indifferent to his party's demands.
The government will soon invite international tender for setting up a thermal power project in Khulna.
Ruling Awami League party MP Bangabir Abdul Kader Siddiqi called an "anti-terrorism" meeting of freedom fighters today in Tangail, cut off for two days by a road transport strike.
Four new export processing zones (EPZs) are going to be set up in Bangladesh by private entrepreneurs, official sources said on Monday.
A "short supply" of little over 100,000 tonnes in Urea distribution in the first six months of the current year (1996-97) may push prices of fertilizer up.
